introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The volume of a sphere is increasing at the rate of $25\pi\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$. Given that the radius of the sphere is 5 cm, find the rate at which

(a) the radius is increasing, *[3 marks]*

[The volume of the sphere, $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$ and the surface area of the sphere, $A=4\pi r^2$]
questions.corrige_markdown:
Given $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=25\pi$. Since $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$, $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2$.

By the chain rule, $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{dV}{dr}\times\dfrac{dr}{dt}$:

$$25\pi=4\pi r^2\,\frac{dr}{dt}.$$

At $r=5$: $25\pi=4\pi(25)\dfrac{dr}{dt}=100\pi\dfrac{dr}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{25\pi}{100\pi}=0.25$.

**The radius is increasing at $0.25\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) the surface area is increasing. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$A=4\pi r^2$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dr}=8\pi r$. By the chain rule:

$$\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}=8\pi(5)\times0.25=10\pi.$$

$10\pi\approx31.4$.

**The surface area is increasing at $10\pi\approx31.4\ \text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) The area bounded by the curve $y^2=x^3$ and the $x$-axis and the lines $x=2$ to $x=4$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of the solid generated. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume of revolution about the $x$-axis is $V=\pi\displaystyle\int_a^b y^2\,dx$. Here $y^2=x^3$, $a=2$, $b=4$:

$$V=\pi\int_2^4x^3\,dx=\pi\left[\frac{x^4}4\right]_2^4=\pi\left(\frac{256}{4}-\frac{16}{4}\right)=\pi(64-4)=60\pi.$$

$60\pi\approx188.5$.

**Volume $=60\pi\approx188.5$ cubic units.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) The position vectors of the centre of gravity of three particles of mass $m$ kg, 5 kg and 3 kg which are at the points with position vectors $3\mathbf i-\mathbf j$, $-6\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$ and $-2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j$ respectively is $-2\mathbf i+a\mathbf j$. Given that $m$ and $a$ are constants, find the values of $m$ and $a$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For particles of masses $m_i$ at position vectors $\mathbf r_i$, the centre of gravity is $\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{\sum m_i\mathbf r_i}{\sum m_i}$. The total mass is $m+5+3=m+8$.

$$(m+8)\bar{\mathbf r}=m(3\mathbf i-\mathbf j)+5(-6\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)+3(-2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)=(3m-36)\mathbf i+(22-m)\mathbf j.$$

**$\mathbf i$ components:** $\dfrac{3m-36}{m+8}=-2\Rightarrow3m-36=-2m-16\Rightarrow5m=20\Rightarrow m=4.$

**$\mathbf j$ components:** $\dfrac{22-m}{m+8}=a$. With $m=4$: $a=\dfrac{18}{12}=\dfrac32.$

Check: $\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{(12-36)\mathbf i+18\mathbf j}{12}=-2\mathbf i+1.5\mathbf j$ ✓.

**$m=4$ and $a=\dfrac32=1.5$.**
